prompt:
I need the front end for Commonwell AI Catalog. A state government's internal ordering service where agency staff enroll their units in AI tools the state IT office has approved, committing seats against their unit's budget under statewide contract terms.

Who's using it: Denise Holloway, office manager for the Unemployment Insurance Appeals unit at the state Department of Labor. She handles purchasing for 34 staff, knows the state's procurement rules well, and is cautious about AI. She's not technical, and she will be the person answering to the fiscal officer if a charge is wrong.

What they're doing right now: Last month she enrolled 15 hearing officers in an approved AI transcription tool on the Standard tier. The pilot went well, and the unit director now wants 12 more seats. But the hearings contain claimant Social Security numbers and medical details, and the state privacy office has just said that data needs the Restricted tier, which costs more and has a 12-month minimum term. Denise has to decide whether to upgrade the existing 15 seats and add 12 at Restricted, or keep Standard for non-confidential work. She needs to confirm the data classification, check the total against her remaining fiscal-year budget, accept the contract terms, and place the order. She also needs to know exactly how long she can cancel without penalty, since the director may change his mind after the budget hearing on 8 December.

What's in the system at this point: 9 approved AI tools. For the transcription tool 'ClearMinute', Standard is $28/seat/month, month-to-month, cleared for Public and Internal data. Restricted is $46/seat/month with a 12-month minimum, cleared up to Confidential/PII, and has a 14-day no-penalty cancellation window after activation. Her unit's cost center is 4410-UIA. Its fiscal year runs July–June, the AI line has $38,400 left, and $2,520 has been spent so far. Existing order #CW-2026-0917: 15 Standard seats, active since 14 Oct 2026, with seat holders named. Order changes need an approval chain (Denise, then the unit director R. Batista, then the fiscal officer). Contract terms are version 2.3, updated 1 Nov 2026.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
